subject: LLM on-prem orchestration — recommended connection workflow (peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN)
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Park <lucy@sableco.com>, Anand Rao <anand.rao@sableco.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: LLM on-prem orchestration — recommended connection workflow (peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN)

Hi Lucy / Anand —

Thanks for the details in the kickoff yesterday. I've sketched a pragmatic path for connecting your on-prem and multi-account cloud footprint to Redwood Private (VPC/private deployment). High-level recommendations up front, followed by a short rollout plan and the tradeoffs table (attached).

Executive summary (short):
- Preferred cross-account / cross-account-account safe option: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for control plane and inference API access when you cannot or will not accept cross-account peering. It avoids public exposure and is compatible with strict network boundaries.
- Preferred intra-org low-latency option: VPC Peering (or Transit Gateway) if both sides can accept peering and overlapping CIDRs are resolved — best for sub-20ms latencies and minimal packet encapsulation.
- On-prem / encrypted WAN: Site-to-site VPN is the pragmatic fallback or for initial POCs; secure but adds jitter and higher latency; use for administrative/control traffic or as an HA path.

Key constraints I need you to confirm before we finalize the design:
1) Will you allow cross-account peering to a Redwood-owned VPC in your region? If not, we should plan PrivateLink.
2) What is your target 95th percentile end-to-end inference latency (ms)? You mentioned <25ms during the call — confirm.
3) Any CIDR overlap between your on-prem / cloud VPCs and Redwood’s suggested endpoints?
4) Compliance: Is PrivateLink required (no public endpoint exposure) for SOC2 / data residency reasons?

Attached: privatelink-vs-peering-vpn-matrix.xlsx (cost/ops/latency checklist) and a rough network diagram (sableco-onprem-network-diagram.png).

Suggested rollout (phased):
1) PrivateLink POC (1-2 days): establish an interface endpoint in your VPC, run small canary traffic to verify DNS + SG policies.
2) Add S2S VPN (if on-prem): configure site-to-site for encrypted fallback and to support admin consoles.
3) If after POC latency is still insufficient and you can accept peering, migrate critical inference dataplane into a peered VPC for the ultra-low-latency path, keeping PrivateLink for the control plane.

Operational notes:
- PrivateLink consumes ENI IPs in the target subnet and has soft limits; we’ll size subnets up front.
- Peering removes NAT overhead but requires route management and no overlapping CIDR.
- VPN adds MTU considerations (fragmentation) and jitter — plan for 10–30ms median overhead depending on endpoint placement.

Next steps: please confirm items 1–4 and add your procurement contact (if different from the Proc email you shared). Once confirmed I’ll send a short SOW/technical appendix and a 45-minute design call invite.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Thanks Michael — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- Latency target: for production inference we need 95th <25ms, ideally <20ms for our high-frequency user flows.
- Accounts: Our infra lives in a different AWS account (security policy currently prevents cross-account peering without an exception).
- Public exposure: procurement/compliance wants no public-facing endpoints for inference calls. PrivateLink seems attractive for that reason.
- On-prem: our DC in Chicago will be the main data ingress; we can add a dedicated S2S VPN but want it as HA/fallback, not the primary.

Can you include an HA dual-path strategy (PrivateLink primary + VPN fallback)? Also, procurement (procure@sableco.com) asked for: a short list of required IP ranges, an ownership checklist, and an initial SOW estimate.

—Lucy
Head of Platform Engineering, SableCo

Subject: Re: LLM on-prem orchestration — recommended connection workflow (peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN)

Lucy — perfect, thanks for the clarity. Given those constraints, here's an updated, practical plan and the specific asks we’ll action immediately: 

Design decisions (mapped to your reqs):
- Primary: PrivateLink interface endpoint in your VPC (no public exposure). PrivateLink satisfies the compliance ask and works cross-account.
- Dataplane performance: Because PrivateLink fronts traffic through ENIs, we expect a modest additional hop. For most workloads with median single-request compute times >> network hop, this is acceptable. For ultra-low-latency (<10ms) inference loops, peering (in same account or with exception) is required — but you indicated an exception is unlikely.
- HA/fallback: S2S IPsec VPN between your Chicago DC and your VPC an S2S to Redwood’s VPN concentrator. Use BGP for route failover.

Concrete deliverables I’ll produce by end of day tomorrow:
1) Required IP ranges (CIDR list) for the PrivateLink ENIs and control IPs; we’ll include recommended subnet sizing.
2) Ownership checklist: security contact, network lead, PKI/KMS owner to perform key exchange for VPN if used.
3) SOW draft: timeline, tasks (endpoint creation, security review, canary, SLA/rollout), and ballpark hours + costs.

Operational notes (short):
- DNS: We recommend using AWS Route 53 private hosted zone or conditional forwarding to resolve the service name to the interface endpoint IPs. We’ll provide an example entry.
- IP consumption: PrivateLink ENIs consume private IPs per AZ. Plan for 3 AZs if you want AZ redundancy — that’s 3 ENIs at minimum.
- Security groups: lock down inbound to only your app subnets and/or on-prem networks; we can provide exact SG rules.
- Observability: Redwood will emit per-route latency and token cost; we’ll include an initial dashboard template in the SOW.

Attachments updated in the drive link. I’ll prepare the SOW and the IP list and loop in Kimberly for the PrivateLink quotas/limits.

Best,
Michael

Quick technical note (lv):
- For inference-serving workloads with large KV cache reuse (long-running sessions), cross-VPC packet hops can impact tail latency due to network jitter. If SableCo later needs sub-10ms tail latency for streaming workloads, we should plan a dataplane migration to a peered VPC in the same region (or colocated account) — PrivateLink is fine for control and occasional requests but peering preserves the lowest possible RTT and fewer TCP handoffs.
- If you go PrivateLink primary, ensure ENI placement across AZs and that you reserve enough IPs for expected ops growth (recommend +30% headroom).
- On VPN: watch MTU and ICMP blackhole issues; add MSS clamping on the tunnel endpoints if you see fragmentation.

I'll add a one-page appendix on latency-sensitive patterns to the SOW.

-Karthik
Senior Network Architect — Redwood Inference
